I very much enjoyed my roughly 40 hour playthrough of this game. And yes, sometimes decried the "unfairness" of the game but then I tried again, changed my strategy or just learned how to properly dodge and all was good. The game seems to have undergone quite a bit of rebalancing since its release and I couldn't find any distinctive spikes in difficulty (unless you tackle optional bosses too early) or problems with the stats system and requirements. The only issue I can fonfirm, is that performance could be better. But real lags only happened in rainy areas for me.

I have mixed feeling about Immortal.  I did finish it, i had some fun with it and the core gameplay is fun. However with that being said there were a lot of "COME ON" moments in this game that were incredible frustrating. There are a lot of chaotic areas in this game with multiple teleporting snipers and enemies shooting at you from all directions and at times it is simply not fun.

Overall it is a competent science fiction dark souls with gun but it is clunkier, less varied and have more annoying moments than the games it is inspired of and the highpoints are less special due to the boring bosses and smaller production values.

This game tries to be Dark Souls with guns. I feel like the learning curve was a little steep in the beginning but I eventually got the hang of what was going on. However, I just never found any really good guns and the upgrades were meh. On top of that, the game crashed on me about 3 times. The final time it took 40K bits(souls) with it and I just had to stop playing. Overall, I just wasn't getting that sense of satisfaction from progression that I got with Dark Souls and Bloodborne.

TLDR: I can only recommend this game to a specific subset of Souls-like fans.

This game is basically Demon's Souls with guns. Much like Demon's Souls in particular, you're going to be expected to crawl and drag yourself from bonfire to bonfire, fighting against not only the enemies along the way but also the game itself. You'll need to be prepared to cleverly abuse game mechanics, exploit terrain in your favor, bait things using line of sight, and engage every encounter on your terms. Expect a lot of cheap deaths, questionable AI, unreasonably quick snipers, and unbalanced difficulty spikes between bonfires. Personally, I'm having a blast.

An excellent first go.

I can't wait to see where Toadman Interactive go next. The reception of Immortal Unchained may be a bit mixed, and for good reasons. The game is janky as hell, and having the shadow detail above low will make you computer collapse in despair. That being said, the gameplay is superb and well-balanced, the boss fights are fun, and the enemy designs are distinct enough that you can immediately understand how they work, and how to best approach them, the areas and general art design are superb, the soundtrack is fantastic, and the weapon variety is nothing to scoff at.
I say all this just having come off the final boss fight. 
TL;DR,
+ Solid gameplay loop.
+ Integration of soulsborne mechanics into a shooter done extremely well.
+ Provides satisfying loot.
+ Offers good build variety for replayability.
+ Enemy design, if a little generic, signals behavior very well.
+ Exploration and going off the beaten path is extremely rewarded. I'm talking hidden bosses, legendary weapons, and keys to chests scattered across the game world.

*- Areas are big. Very big. And there are only three. You might get bored of a single continuous aesthetic depending on your attention span. 
*- Crosshair takes getting used to. Just remember that nothing is hitscan, and bullets come from the barrel of your gun. Your crosshair will turn red if you can hit an enemy.

- Bosses easier than some standard enemies.
- Shadows will tank FPS. Turn them off for the best performance.
- Ending is a bit silly.

If you crave a soulsborne game and/or a looter shooter, pick this up when it goes on sale. It's worth between $15 and $20 USD in its current state.

Got this game on sale for $12. So, for Toadman's first game, it isn't bad, but definitely is flawed and could use numerous updates. As for the game, like most have pointed out, its a Souls-esque game with guns. However, the dodge mechanics and AI could use a major overhaul. Enemies don't move much from their spots, which can leave you in tight situations where you get killed because of the game mechanics, and not because it is hard. The classes, moreover, do not provide much variety and leave one begging for more. Overall the game is fun, so pick it up on sale and give Toadman the chance to make this game one worth having in your library.

I picked up this one on sale and it is a good game but damn if it doesn't have some issues.  

Yes, as the other reviews say, it is a souls-like game. It's harsh and often unforgiving. I think the problem here is balance. 
I'll speak on that more further down. TLDR version at the bottom.

The good points (remember this is subjective): 
Compelling Story - I actually was motivated to finish it in spite of the flaw. It's not complex or deep but the world, gunplay, and visuals are good. 
The graphics are really good. A bit dark in some places and I know there are paint kits for the armor but I didn't really notice any difference when I applied them.
The combat is pretty fun when it works properly. For the 11 bucks I paid, I enjoyed it - with a few exceptions below. 
The monolith save points are frequent and make it fairly easy to get back into the game. 

The Bad points (again subjective) - 
Movement is smooth until it isn't. Maybe it was just me but there were points I felt like my character got hung up on the level geometry. With no actual jump button this gets frustrating and leads into the next point. 
The level design is good but some levels are really hard to navigate with uneven levels which makes you get stuck here and there with no way to jump. You can roll but this can send you over a bottomless edge, often.
The aiming in the game is ok with the sniper rifles, everything else is really iffy. 

The UGLY (yes subjective, mostly)

These may end up being what turns most away from the game. It almost did with me. 

The sheer difficulty of this game. This game was tougher on me than I think even the original Demon Souls (I think that was the name of the Precursor to Dark Souls?) was. 

I got through about half the game before I went seeking a trainer. In part to finish the game and in part because I wanted to test a few things. I do fully believe this game can be completed without one but I don't think I would have spent the time on it. Think of one step forward and two steps back. - I was over 11 hours in and on my third character. 

Knockback/Stun - No matter how high you bump up your stats, this remains a problem. 
One hit kills - these happen, again, no matter how high your stats or hitpoints 
Most of the game really relies on you upgrading your weapons. 
Armor points and other stats really didn't seem to matter until I bumped my character's HP to around 1000 - level 300+
Overuse of some mechanics. One being the things that grab your character and hold them in place. You first see this on the first big boss. The next level after them is ridiculously riddled with them. Seriously. 
Teleporting enemies. In the late game these guys will waste you fast. This needs to be toned down. 
Enemy grenades. Again, even in the earliest areas of the game the enemy throws a grenade way more often than it should. 
You often don't even see enemies that spawn on ledges above you and then drop grenades.
Your stats do not seem to affect how well your guns aim.  

TLDR - It's a game that can be unforgiving but fun. 
If you can get it on sale and you don't mind a really challenging game get it. 
Find a trainer. Unlimited Ammo, No Reload, and unlimited healing charges will make things a lot more fun. I almost hate to recommend a cheat to make a game fun but it does. 
You can beat it without downloading a trainer but expect a lot of frustration. 
It is NOT a bad game at all. It's just not very well balanced. 
I really hated not recommending it because at least some of the difficulty is my lack of skill but there are some elements that just really kill the game for me.

From Swedish developer/publisher Toadman Interactive comes their first full release, Immortal: Unchained; a Souls-like game that trades traditional weapons for guns, and a fantasy setting for a futuristic sci-fi theme. Taking place in an alternate universe that's heavily inspired by Norse mythology, the game puts players in the role of an unnamed prisoner who is afflicted with amnesia; a side-effect of their long-term imprisonment. Their release comes at a cost, that they must help prevent the coming of the end times by repairing the Monolith, a stone artifact at the center of the universe that controls the Nine Worlds.

While the lore of Immortal: Unchained may sound interesting in writing, discovering it all in the game is another story. Players must hunt and find three different types of lore items to slowly piece everything together, painstakingly. Everything is written under the assumption that the audience is well aware of the names of unmet, and unintroduced, characters and locations. Without consulting a Wiki, spending hours collecting lore, and even more time sewing it all together, most gamers will only have a small idea of what's going on. The plot is overly intricate and too convoluted to casually enjoy. Not to mention, most of these lore items are found in enemy-infested areas, and audiences are rushed to read the text rather than taking the time to absorb it.

The gameplay is as anyone would expect from a Souls-like. There are Obelisks that allow for leveling up, weapon upgrading and management, artifact discovering, and even fast travel that's unlocked at a much later stage. Up to four weapons and a melee item can be carried in the quick-selection menu, but each slot is unlocked via story progression. There's almost a Diablo/World of Warcraft style loot system, where opening up containers can yield players with common, uncommon, rare, and legendary items. Every weapon can be upgraded as well, but be prepared to spend time exploring every nook and cranny for boxes containing the required parts; as well as a ton of time grinding out unfathomable amounts of Forgotten Bits, which work like Souls, in order to level up.

Much like Demon's Souls, the world of Immortal: Unchained is split up into multiple levels which are accessed via portals; the snowy planet of Arden, the forest of Veridian, and the abandoned Prime home planet Apexion. These three planets start out rather small, but after the first half of the game, they expand into much bigger areas. Their designs are rather complex, but each world is interesting for a short period of time; thereafter, they start to feel boring due to the mass amount of backtracking that is required. However, the soundtrack is rich and incredible, and it's well worth it to turn down the sound effects just so it can be enjoyed by itself. In fact, it's one of the highlights of the release, and it's available for free on the store page.

Immortal: Unchained does have a lot of good ideas behind it; giving guns to a Souls-like game is an extremely intriguing concept, especially coupling it with a futuristic sci-fi setting. It's unfortunate that there are so many irritating flaws that keep the game from reaching its full potential. One of the major problems here is the lack of optimization, to the point that several key areas of this release run at around 22-26 FPS at 1080p on an i7-6700k/GTX 1080 rig. Areas that were nearly impossible to get past due to the massive amounts of stuttering and slow motion that occurred, while trying to fight off some of the toughest enemies in the game. This is completely unacceptable, especially when taking into consideration that the developer chose to work on paid DLC content instead of fixing known issues.

Additionally, the enemy AI skates between being abysmally stupid and normal. A lot of the time, foes will just stand there and let you pummel them; even some mini-bosses. There's something screwy with the reticle where the bullets don't quite line up, instead, every gun shoots slightly to the left of the reticle. Last but not least, the game-breaking feature that made me quit playing before I actually finished the campaign: during a very plot-heavy boss fight, real life called to me and I had to shut the game off since there is no pause button. Later, when I booted the game up, the boss fight had been skipped, along with all of the end-game plot, and I was thrown into some labyrinth going through portal after portal. Since I missed the entire end of the game, or the biggest plot point that was leading to it, there was no reason for me to even continue. 

Essentially, the TL;DR here is that Immortal: Unchained has a great amalgamation of ideas, but poor and shoddy execution is its ultimate downfall. The developer has been told about many of these issues time and time again, yet still there is DLC coming in May instead of an optimization update, or fixes to some really concerning bugs like the off-center gunfire. It's a shame really, since much of Immortal: Unchained is fairly fun, despite its unpolished nature; a lot of the smaller gripes could even be overlooked. That said, there are just too many problems here that make for a very frustrating experience. It's suggested to just skip this one in lieu of the real Dark Souls series, or perhaps Nioh.

As is becoming a tradition with me, I once again have experienced zero of the bugs I'm seeing people complain about. 

Anyways, I really don't know how I feel about this game at the 2 hour mark. The only reason I'm not completely sure about refunding it is because i got it for ~10 bucks. If I'd paid full price, I'd be refunding it no question. The game is... it's okay? 
Like, the guns are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ sweet, the bosses have been fun so far, but the standard enemies are just so... dull. And the standard enemies are 90% of the game, obviously. Everything else about the game is good. The level design, the bosses, the weapons... But when the most important part of the game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks it drags the rest of the game down with it.

I guess I can say if you can get this for ~10 dollars do it, but watch a lot of gameplay videos first to make sure it's for you.

At full price, I do not recommend this game. Sorry, Toadman. I hope you guys learn from the mixed reception of this game and use it to create something even greater rather than just giving up, because there's a LOT of potential here. 
For what it's worth, this is way better than LoTF or The Surge.

I had a lot of fun with this game. It's rough around the edges, and it certainly has its problems, but when it works well, it really works well. I definitely got that souls buzz, but with the pleasure of having to engage with a totally different combat rhythm to Souls / Soulslikes. I genuinely think a lot of the negativity stems from people who don't appreciate that this is a soulslike, and are expecting a shooter. It doesn't articulate like Gears of War, and if you expect it to, you will bounce off it immediately.

I'm really happy with this game.  I've enjoyed most of the level design.  I actually was more impressed with this souls like than many other 3D souls-likes (i.e., the surge).  Interestingly, I never play with ranged weapons or spells in Dark Souls, but I really did enjoy most of the guns and the style of play in this game.  I do wish the melee was a bit deeper.  But overall, I do recommend this game if you are interested in souls like or technomancer fiction.
